key_insight: Mathematical reasoning in LLMs is limited less by final-answer accuracy than by a missing structural primitive, with Discovery emerging as the main bottleneck and the most repairable failure mode.
engineering_relevance: For building more reliable reasoning models, the work suggests post-training should target primitive-level capabilities—especially discovery—rather than only optimizing outcome accuracy.
method: Defined a "Mathematical Primitive" to probe structural understanding.
Introduced \hlei{}, a benchmark spanning Discovery, Generation, Digestion, and Execution.
Built \abs{}, a primitive-privileged self-distillation framework that transfers primitive-guided reasoning to a student model.
evidence_signal: The paper reports systematic diagnosis across a four-dimension benchmark plus post-training experiments, showing primitives can unlock latent execution capacity and that discovery-limited failures are especially amenable to repair.
watch_item: The framework depends on reliable primitive-level supervision and benchmark design, so gains may be sensitive to how well the discovery signals generalize beyond the evaluated math tasks.
paper_title: The Missing Primitive: Diagnosing and Repairing Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
